title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day Crosses Rs 15 Crore in India Presales With 12 Days Still to Go
excerpt: Tom Holland's fourth solo Spider-Man film is on track for the second-biggest Hollywood opening day in India, with PVRINOX selling over 200,000 weekend tickets and Prasads in Hyderabad already sold out.
body:
• Spider-Man: Brand New Day has crossed Rs 15 crore in advance bookings for its opening weekend in India, with Rs 5 crore from the first day alone
  • PVRINOX has sold 76,000 tickets worth Rs 4 crore for day one and over 200,000 tickets totaling Rs 11.50 crore for the weekend
  • The film is forecast to open between Rs 40-48 crore nett, potentially the second-biggest Hollywood opening day ever in India after Avengers: Endgame
  • Standard format bookings opened just yesterday, and several major centers and cinema chains have not yet started sales

Presales Surge Past Rs 15 Crore

Spider-Man: Brand New Day is building toward what could be the biggest Hollywood opening in India since Avengers: Endgame, with advance ticket sales crossing Rs 15 crore for the opening weekend and the film still 12 days from its July 30 release date.

The numbers are striking. PVRINOX, India's largest cinema chain, has sold 76,000 tickets worth Rs 4 crore for the first day alone, with the weekend tally reaching over 200,000 tickets at Rs 11.50 crore. Cinepolis has added another 14,000 first-day tickets. Premium properties in South India are running near capacity. Prasads in Hyderabad, one of the country's most iconic multiplexes, is sold out on day one and nearly full for the rest of the opening weekend.

BookMyShow, India's dominant ticketing platform, sold 44,000 tickets in a single day when standard format bookings went live, bringing its cumulative total to nearly 175,000 tickets.

On Track to Challenge Endgame's Record

Industry trackers forecast an opening day between Rs 40-48 crore nett, which would make Brand New Day the second-biggest Hollywood debut in Indian box office history. The all-time record belongs to Avengers: Endgame, which opened at Rs 53.50 crore in 2019.

What makes the advance booking numbers especially notable is timing. Standard format bookings, which account for the bulk of India's theatrical audience, only opened on July 17. Several major cities and cinema chains have not yet begun selling tickets. Premium formats like IMAX remain unavailable for the film, as Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey holds a multi-week IMAX exclusivity deal.

"It cannot be overstated that there are still almost two weeks to go for release, and the fact that the film has already gathered these pre-sales underlines the immense buzz it is carrying."

— Pinkvilla Box Office Tracking

A Changed Market Since No Way Home

The previous Spider-Man film, No Way Home, opened at Rs 32.70 crore in December 2021, impressive for a market still recovering from COVID lockdowns. Since then, India's theatrical business has expanded significantly, particularly in Southern states. The Telugu-speaking Andhra Pradesh and Telangana markets, along with Karnataka and Kerala, have shown stronger Hollywood consumption.

Hollywood has also been on an unusual hot streak in India this year, with multiple unexpected successes building audience confidence in theatrical releases. Brand New Day is one of the few expected blockbusters, and the presales suggest it will deliver.

What to Watch

With standard bookings now open nationwide and 12 days of sales remaining, the trajectory points toward a Rs 40 crore-plus opening. If late-week momentum builds, trackers have not ruled out a run at the Rs 50 crore mark. For Indian audiences and the NRI community watching the film's global rollout, Brand New Day is shaping up to be the event Hollywood release of the summer.
